hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea and Liberia || coastal belt of mangrove swamps, wooded hill country, upland plateau, mountains in east || rainfall along the coast can reach 495 cm (195 in) a year, making it one of the wettest places along coastal western Africa || Resources: diamonds, titanium ore, bauxite, iron ore, gold, chromite || Exports: iron ore, titanium ore, diamonds, aluminum ore, cocoa beans (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: coastal belt of mangrove swamps, wooded hill country, upland plateau, mountains in east || Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Guinea and Liberia

climate.excerpt: tropical; hot, humid; summer rainy season (May to December); winter dry season (December to April) || dry, sand-laden harmattan winds blow from the Sahara (December to February); sandstorms, dust storms

economy.excerpt: low-income West African economy; primarily subsistent agriculture; key iron and diamond mining activities suspended; slow recovery from 1990s civil war; systemic corruption; high-risk debt; high youth unemployment; natural resource rich || Exports: iron ore, titanium ore, diamonds, aluminum ore, cocoa beans (2023) || Industries: diamond mining; iron ore, rutile and bauxite mining; small-scale manufacturing (beverages, textiles, footwear)

peopleAndCulture.from: People and Society > Languages, Religions, Ethnic groups, Urbanization
peopleAndCulture.excerpt: English (official, regular use limited to literate minority), Mende (principal vernacular in the south), Temne (principal vernacular in the north), Krio (English-based Creole, spoken by the descendants of freed Jamaican slaves; a first language for 10% of the population but understood by 95%) || Muslim 77.1%, Christian 22.9% (2019 est.) || Temne 35.4%, Mende 30.8%, Limba 8.8%, Kono 4.3%, Korankoh 4%, Fullah 3.8%, Mandingo 2.8%, Loko 2%, Sherbro 1.9%, Creole 1.2% (descendants of freed Jamaican slaves who were settled in the Freetown area in the late-18th century; also known as Krio), other 5% (2019 est.)
